subject: System Design
title: Leaderless Replication
description: A quick, practical guide to Leaderless Replication.

hook.text: In Cassandra, there's no leader at all. Writes go to any node. Reads check multiple nodes for the latest value.

buildup.text: Leaderless replication writes to W nodes and reads from R nodes. If W + R > N, you get consistency.

discovery.text: Quorum reads and writes ensure at least one node has the latest value, even without a leader.

twist.text: With sloppy quorums, even W + R > N doesn't guarantee consistency. Edge cases abound.

climax.text: Leaderless systems maximize availability but require careful tuning of W, R, and N for your use case.

punchline.text: No leader, quorum-based — available but tricky.

quiz.question: What ensures consistency in leaderless replication?
options: W + R > N where W is writes, R is reads, N is total nodes
